'''''Aeonium glutinosum''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]] endemic to [[Madeira]], [[Portugal]]. It has fairly thick leaves and its appearance varies depending on its growing conditions. One characteristic is the very sticky stem of the inflorescence. The main flower is shown but small stalks with flowers continue to appear for several months.

==Description==
It is a very viscous perennial sub-shrub, with a robust stem, branches up to {{convert|60|cm|in}} decumbent or ascending, occasionally [[Sessility (botany)|subsessile]] plants. [[Rosette (design)|Rosette]]-shaped leaves up to {{convert|22|cm|in}} in diameter with loose, subtle young leaves. Leaves up to {{convert|12|x|5|cm|in}}, yellowish-green, usually with brownish stripes near the apex, glabrous, ciliated margins with few or numerous thin single-celled hairs. Inflorescences very loose, remotely branched, up to {{convert|40|x|45|cm|in}} Petals {{convert|5|-|7|mm|in}}, golden yellow, usually with red stripes abaxially.<ref name="uma">{{cite web |title=Aeonium glutinosum (Ait.) Webb et Berthel. |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=178 |website=www3.uma.pt |access-date=28 November 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is [[endemic]] to [[Madeira Island]] and [[Deserta Grande Island]] part of the [[Madeira|Madeira Archipelago]].<ref name="uma" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Species Details : Aeonium glutinosum (Ait.) Webb & Berth. |url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/col/details/species/id/35a91daa8d1b1ed3970caafc5fac76f0 |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>
